ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, O is a point on the line AB, $\angle AOC=50^\circ$, OD bisects $\angle AOC$, and $\angle DOE=90^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle COD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle AOC=50^\circ$ and $OD$ bisects $\angle AOC$,

$\therefore \angle COD=\angle DOA= \frac{1}{2}\angle AOC=\boxed{25^\circ}$,

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, AB is a straight line passing through O, A is on the left side of O, and B is on the right side of O; from O toward the upper left there are two rays OC and OD, among which OD is located between OA and OC, so ∠COD is one of the two angles into which OD divides ∠AOC. Ray OE is in the upper right, and has no direct relation to ∠COD required by this problem. Then reason: It is known that ∠AOC = 50°, and OD bisects ∠AOC. Because OD is the angle bisector, ∠COD = ∠DOA = 50° ÷ 2 = 25°.
